paragraphs: Here's what gets me, friend. Gideon says the right thing. The people offer him the crown, and he answers, "The LORD shall rule over you." (Judges 8:23) Then he takes all that gold and makes an ephod, and Israel ends up worshiping it. It became "a snare to Gideon and his household." (Judges 8:27)

So here's the lesson, baker. Saying the right words is one thing, and what we build with our hands is another. A good start doesn't keep a heart pointed at the LORD all by itself. What we make from our wins can pull people's eyes off Him, even when we didn't mean it to. I've had a cookie turn out so pretty that I stared at the cookie and forgot to thank the One who gave me the oven.

And look at what happens when Gideon is gone. "The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side." (Judges 8:34) Forty years of rest, and still they forgot. So remembering is a daily job, friend. Keep thanking Him for what He's done, because the One who rescued you is the One worth worshiping. And this story isn't over, so keep that apron tied.
